feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
entry.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

entry.title: The price tag for the Iran war has hit over $30B, reports say
entry.summary: Two new reports detail the damage the Iran war has caused to U.S. bases and the rising cost of the war, which has hit over $30 billion.

entry.title: U.S. acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space
entry.summary: The remarkable revelation comes after previous warnings about countries such as Russia possibly weaponizing a global frontier long agreed in treaties to be used for only peaceful purposes.

entry.title: 3 people killed when news helicopter crashes while covering LA bus accident
entry.summary: A news helicopter used by NBC and Telemundo crashed in a Los Angeles neighborhood on Tuesday, killing at least three people while reporters were covering the nearby crash of an SUV and a city bus.

entry.title: Judge blocks DHS from acting against a man over a harsh email to an ICE official
entry.summary: ICE agents turned up at David Streever's home over a harsh email he sent to an ICE official. Now a court order prevents the federal government from making additional threats against him.

entry.title: Prosecutors won't seek the death penalty for Nick Reiner
entry.summary: Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said his office spoke with Reiner's siblings and took their wishes into consideration in the decision.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI
entry.summary: The rare pairing of a progressive leader and a MAGA voice is a sign of how worries over rapidly advancing AI are upending political alliances. But their policy proposals are far apart.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: President Trump downplays fears about AI risks, Supreme Court rejects Trump's efforts to enact mail-in voting restrictions for the midterms, Kennedy Center says it's on the brink of bankruptcy.

entry.title: Supreme Court refuses to allow Trump's mail voting restrictions for the midterms
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected President Trump's push for new mail-in voting restrictions for the midterm election.

entry.title: Attorney discusses the Kennedy Center's financial woes and Trump's naming efforts
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez talks to Attorney Greg Werkheiser, of the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, about Trump's efforts to add his name to the Kennedy Center and the financial trouble it's facing.
